Description: Low-Rank Adaptation. Freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects small trainable rank-decomposition matrices into each transformer layer. Reduces trainable parameters by ~99% vs full fine-tuning, making it feasible to fine-tune large LLMs on a single GPU.
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Core fine-tuning technique for per-tenant memo generation models. Each VC client gets their own LoRA adapter (a small ~50-300MB file) trained on their analyst memos, stored in S3 and loaded on top of a shared base model at inference time.
Short File/Config Template:
# lora_config.py
from peft import LoraConfig

config = LoraConfig(
    r=16,                    # rank — higher = more capacity
    lora_alpha=32,           # scaling factor
    target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"],
    lora_dropout=0.05,
    bias="none",
    task_type="CAUSAL_LM"
)

Description: Quantized LoRA. Extends LoRA by quantizing the frozen base model to 4-bit precision (using NF4 data type), dramatically reducing VRAM usage. Allows fine-tuning a 70B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU that would otherwise require multiple A100s.
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Used when fine-tuning larger base models (LLaMA 3 70B, Mixtral) for high-value tenants who need better quality. Enables cost-effective training on smaller GPU instances on Modal or RunPod.
Short File/Config Template:
# qlora_setup.py
from transformers import BitsAndBytesConfig
import torch

bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16
)
# Pass bnb_config to AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained()

Description: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning library by Hugging Face. Implements LoRA, QLoRA, Prefix Tuning, and other efficient adaptation methods. The standard Python library for attaching and training LoRA adapters on top of HF models.
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Used in the fine-tuning pipeline (Modal/RunPod jobs) to apply LoRA configs to base models, train on tenant data, and save adapter weights. Also used at inference to load the correct tenant adapter on top of the shared base model.
Short File/Config Template:
# peft_train.py
from peft import get_peft_model, LoraConfig
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM

base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1")
peft_config = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
model = get_peft_model(base_model, peft_config)
model.print_trainable_parameters()
# Trainable params: 4,194,304 || All params: 3,752,071,168 (~0.11%)

Description: Elastic Kubernetes Service — AWS managed Kubernetes. Runs containerized workloads with auto-scaling, rolling deployments, and service discovery. Standard choice for production microservices on AWS.
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Runs the core platform services: FastAPI orchestration layer, document pipeline workers, reranking services, vLLM inference servers. Enables per-tenant namespace isolation, horizontal scaling of API pods during pitch deck processing peaks, and zero-downtime deployments.

Description: Elastic Container Service — AWS simpler alternative to Kubernetes. Runs Docker containers without managing Kubernetes control plane. Lower operational overhead, tighter AWS integration (Fargate serverless option).
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Recommended starting point before EKS — lower ops burden for a small team. Runs the same FastAPI and worker containers. Migrate to EKS when you need more control (custom scheduling, per-tenant namespaces, advanced networking). Good for async Celery workers on Fargate.

Description: Enterprise feature flag and experimentation platform. Allows toggling features per user, tenant, or percentage rollout without code deployments. Supports A/B testing and gradual rollouts.
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Controls which tenants see new features (e.g. new memo generation model, new screening UI). Allows rolling out a new fine-tuned model to one VC client for validation before broad release. Also used for kill switches on experimental LLM features without redeployment.

Description: Observability platform built specifically for LLM applications by LangChain. Traces every LLM call with inputs, outputs, latency, token usage, and cost. Supports prompt versioning and dataset management for evals.
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Traces all LLM calls in the orchestration layer: which prompt version was used, what context was retrieved, what the model returned, how long it took, and what it cost. Essential for debugging poor memo quality, tracking prompt regressions, and building eval datasets from production traces.
Short File/Config Template:
# langsmith_setup.py
import os
os.environ["LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2"] = "true"
os.environ["LANGCHAIN_API_KEY"] = "ls-key"
os.environ["LANGCHAIN_PROJECT"] = "vc-assistant-prod"

# All subsequent LangChain calls are auto-traced
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic
llm = ChatAnthropic(model="claude-sonnet-4-6")
response = llm.invoke("Screen this pitch deck: ...")
# Trace appears automatically in LangSmith UI

Description: Open-source alternative to LangSmith. Self-hostable LLM observability: traces, prompt management, evals, and cost tracking. Strong privacy story since you can run it in your own VPC — relevant when clients are sensitive about their queries being logged externally.
Role in VC Assistant Infrastructure: Same role as LangSmith but preferred when client data sovereignty is a requirement (self-hosted in your AWS VPC). Tracks LLM traces per tenant with tenant-level dashboards for cost allocation. Also manages prompt versions across environments.
